about: The DD Framework rulebook. Each rule has an id, the incident or source it comes from, the repo kinds it applies to, and two dates: from warn_from it is reported, from enforce_from it fails. enforce_from is at most 90 days after warn_from, so nothing warns forever. lib/rules.mjs holds the checks; test/fixtures.mjs holds a failing and a passing example of every rule, and the tests fail if a rule has none. Exemptions: README, 'Exemptions'.

rules.title: A job in a private Doman-Digital repo names a GitHub-hosted runner directly
rules.why: 2 October 2026: twelve jobs hard-coded to ubuntu-latest used the organisation's hosted minutes and could not move to the self-hosted VM. Use runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}. Only repos owned by Doman-Digital are checked: the runners are registered to the organisation, so a repo in a client's or a personal account cannot use them. A job that hosted-jobs.json pins to a hosted label (runs_on, with a why) is exempt: the runner valve watches the self-hosted runners and must not run on them (DOM-1079).

rules.title: A public repo runs jobs on the self-hosted runners
rules.why: GitHub: never use self-hosted runners with public repositories; a fork's pull request could run code on the VM.

rules.title: A job has no timeout-minutes
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was missing-timeout).

rules.title: A pull_request workflow has no concurrency group that cancels superseded runs
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was missing-concurrency).

rules.title: A workflow runs on both push and pull_request for the same branches
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was double-run). Not reported when a workflow_run deploy waits for the workflow: the push run is the deploy's gate, which CI-014 requires on every push to main (DOM-776).

rules.title: continue-on-error: true with no comment saying why
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit: three permanently red jobs ran unnoticed for months (was unexplained-continue-on-error).

rules.title: A scheduled workflow is not registered in budget.yml
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was unregistered-cron). Fixed 2026-10-03: only the first cron under schedule: was ever read.

rules.title: An artifact upload can fail the job when the storage quota is full
rules.why: 2 October 2026: a 360 MB build uploaded on every run used the organisation's artifact storage for the month, and every PR failed at the upload. Pass builds between jobs another way; mark diagnostic uploads continue-on-error with a comment.

rules.title: A vercel.json cron is not registered in budget.yml
rules.why: 2026-08-16 portfolio audit (was unregistered-vercel-cron).

rules.title: A run on a push to main is cancelled by the next push
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): dd-relay's CI cancelled its own main run on every merge (group ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true). Deploy waits for a successful CI run, so a burst of merges left nothing deployed and a fix went out hours after it merged. Cancel superseded pull request runs only.

rules.title: A production deploy is not serialised, or can be cancelled halfway
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): a deploy that a newer push cancels can leave a Worker updated and its secrets or migrations not, and two deploys at once can finish in the wrong order. One concurrency group per environment with cancel-in-progress: false; a waiting deploy is still replaced by a newer one.

rules.title: A deploy can ship a commit CI did not test, or one older than main
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): once main CI is never cancelled, several runs finish in any order and each starts a deploy. A deploy checks out the commit its CI run tested (workflow_run.head_sha) and stops when that commit is no longer the tip of main, so the last deploy is always the newest tested commit.

rules.title: A repo that calls the policy check runs a scanner of its own
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): the monorepo's secret-scan job and three client repos' gitleaks and TruffleHog jobs each scanned the same commits as the policy check, a full-history clone and another VM for a one-second scan. The monorepo's alone was about 1,350 VM-minutes a month, on a pool of six VMs. From 20 October (step 5) the estate has one scanner per kind of commit: the policy check for pull requests (gitleaks, plus Semgrep for the repos in scanners.json) and the estate sweep in dd-repo-registry for default branches (new commits daily, all history weekly). Any other scanner workflow, whatever starts it, is a duplicate.

rules.title: A workflow still works around the persistent runners
rules.why: DOM-555 replaced the eight runners sharing dd-ci-01 with a fresh VM per job. Port offsets from the runner's name, a pnpm folder per runner, workspace clean-ups and hand-off folders on the host now do nothing, or lose what they keep, and the comments around them describe a machine that is gone (DOM-776 audit: the monorepo, osint-engine and two other repos).

rules.title: A job that runs on every pull request is allowed to fail
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): visual-regression-portal in the monorepo and osint-engine's integration-tests ran on every PR push with continue-on-error: true. Each took a VM from a pool of six, often for minutes, and a red result changed nothing. Advisory work belongs on a schedule or a manual run.

rules.title: A schedule fires on the hour
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): GitHub started scheduled runs 4 to 9.5 hours late, and its documentation says runs at the start of an hour are the most likely to be delayed or dropped. Crons at minute 0 across the estate then queued together on the shared pool.

rules.title: A scheduled workflow works out its batch from the clock
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): Market-probability-engine's Tiingo batches chose their tickers from the hour the run started. GitHub started the runs hours late, so from 8 October every batch picked an empty slot and refreshed nothing, while every run passed.

rules.title: Three or more pull request jobs each install the same dependencies
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776 audit): on the shared pool each job waits for its own VM, then boots, checks out and installs before it does seconds of work. client repos ran 5 to 11 jobs per push, each installing the same lockfile; in the monorepo 58% of job time was setup. One job with several steps does the same checks with one wait and one install.

rules.title: Post-deploy checks start a separate runner for a request
rules.why: DOM-776 audit pattern10: sleeping and requesting DD Checks as a separate reusable-workflow job pays another VM boot and queue wait. Use the composite action as a step after deployment; retain the legacy workflow for callers until they migrate.

rules.title: A job is on the wrong runner pool for its timeout
rules.why: DOM-834, 19 October 2026: about 700 jobs a week finished in under 2 minutes but each held a 4-vCPU VM on a host with 16 (the monorepo's changes job 204 a week at a median of 0.65 minutes, its gate 204 at 0.17). The rulebook decides the pool, not the repo: a job whose timeout-minutes is 5 or less runs on the light pool, runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER_LIGHT || vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}; a longer job, one with service containers or one whose timeout is an expression stays on ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}. A light job that runs out of time is a job whose timeout was wrong: raise it and it moves back. dd adopt writes the fix.

rules.title: A deploy job is not on the deploy slot
rules.why: DOM-834, 20 October 2026: deploys waited in the same queue as pull request CI. dd-relay's deploy sat queued from 11:28 UTC behind 72 PR jobs, so a merged Worker was not live; org deploys (about 60 a week, 1.4 to 5 minutes) waited up to 84 to 215 minutes at p95. A job whose name says deploy (not a dry run or a preview, not in a pull request workflow) runs on its own reserved slot: runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER_DEPLOY || vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}. cloudflare-deploy.yml reads the same variable. dd adopt writes the fix.

rules.title: A caller of the shared deploy does not grant actions: write
rules.why: DOM-1422, 27 October 2026: cloudflare-deploy.yml stops an older commit with a step, so GitHub reported the run as a success a few seconds after it started, and dd-relay's settle() read it as proof a merge was live (DOM-1362). A run that did start can end as something other than a success only by being cancelled, and cancelling needs actions: write, which a called workflow cannot ask for (GitHub refuses to start it) and so only the caller's deploy job can grant. A caller without it still deploys; a superseded run just keeps reporting success. dd adopt --only CI-030 writes the line.

rules.title: A workflow checks who wrote a commit
rules.why: DOM-1451, founder, 27 October 2026: the commit-author checks were a Vercel-era necessity (Vercel refused to build a preview for a commit author outside the client's Vercel team) and are no longer needed. A client repo's enforce-commit-author.yml was the last one; on 27 October a squash merge there turned its push-to-main run red for a commit nothing was wrong with. Author and committer addresses are self-asserted, so a check on them proves nothing about who wrote the code. A workflow that reads a commit's author or committer to pass or fail it comes back only by mistake. GitHub's own refusal of a push carrying a private address is a different rule and stays (dd-claude-kit config/git-identity.json).

rules.title: A shared workflow or action is pinned to a commit no branch or tag holds
rules.why: Doman-Digital/dd-relay#350, 8 November 2026: dd-relay's deploy.yml called cloudflare-deploy.yml at 50504488, a commit dd-ci-standards' rewritten history no longer contained (main carries the same change as 0ee9985). GitHub answered "workflow was not found" at startup, no job ran and nothing alerted, so the relay stayed on its 31 October build for six days. The commit is still served by SHA, so only reachability from a branch or tag is evidence: the doctor asks GitHub (compare default...sha, then the other branches and tags) once per pin per run. A pin it cannot resolve, such as a private repo the token cannot read, is a note, not a finding.

rules.title: CI runs Lighthouse
rules.why: Founder, 15 November 2026 (DOM-17811): Lighthouse is no longer part of CI, for the independence of our machines. Performance, accessibility, best-practice and SEO scores come only from PageSpeed against the deployed URL after the deploy (psi-gate@v1, dd-psi), because a lab run on a shared runner measures the runner: one client site's build measured LCP 2.1 to 3.1 seconds inside a single job while PageSpeed read 1.65 seconds (DOM-17734). Accessibility in CI is axe. A workflow fails this rule when a line it runs uses Lighthouse CI (lhci, @lhci/cli, treosh/lighthouse-ci-action), unlighthouse, the lighthouse CLI, or installs the lighthouse package; and a repo fails it when it keeps a Lighthouse CI config (lighthouserc.*) at its root. A script that calls the PageSpeed API, whatever its file is called, is not Lighthouse on our machine. Warn from 15 November, enforced from 22 November, so open pull requests have a week.

rules.title: A PageSpeed workflow is named like a deploy
rules.why: DOM-17811, 15 November 2026: dd-relay reads any workflow whose name or file mentions deploy as a deploy (src/github-webhook/deploy-alert.ts). A client site's psi-gate workflow was named "PageSpeed after deploy", so a slow page would have paged #alerts as a failed release, and a green run, one job ending success, could have counted as a deploy and moved a Linear issue to Done. A workflow that runs psi-gate measures a deploy; it is not one. Name it without the word ("PageSpeed live").

rules.title: A workflow has no priced row in budget.yml
rules.why: Founder, 15 November 2026 (DOM-17682, programme DOM-17629): GitHub Actions spend is held at or below 60% of the $300 monthly allowance, about $180, and CI must not quietly grow back. November's first 15 days billed $54 (Doman-Digital $33.93 of it), and nothing recorded what any workflow was supposed to cost, so a new workflow, a new trigger or a wider path filter added spend nobody had agreed. Every workflow that starts a run on its own has a row under its repo's `workflows:` in budget.yml: workflow, events, runner_class (hosted-linux, hosted-macos or box), per_run_usd, runs_a_month, owner and reason. The rule fails a workflow with no row, a row missing any of those, and an event the row does not list. A workflow that is only called by another (workflow_call) is priced in its caller's row. test/budget.test.mjs sums the rows against the budget. A widened path filter is not yet seen by this rule (the row has no paths field): re-price the row in the same change. Warn from 15 November, enforced from 29 November, so every caller sees a warning for two weeks first.

rules.title: A budget.yml row prices a workflow or an event that is gone
rules.why: 15 November 2026 (DOM-17682): a priced row that outlives its workflow keeps counting against the monthly budget and hides real headroom, the same drift CI-026 catches for crons. The rule fails a workflows: row whose file no longer exists, whose workflow is now only called by another (workflow_call), or that lists an event the workflow no longer starts on.

rules.title: A job over ten minutes runs on every pull request push
rules.why: 15 November 2026 (DOM-17682): the monorepo billed thousands of hosted minutes in the first 15 days, and a job of 20 to 75 minutes on every push to a pull request pays that again on every fixup commit. A job whose timeout-minutes is over 10 runs on merge to main, in a merge queue or on a schedule, never on every pull request push: give it an `if:` on github.event_name that excludes pull_request, or a "queue" entry in the workflow's tier map (Doman-Digital ci.yml TIERS, DOM-17637). timeout-minutes is a cap, so the rule reads the cap: a job that must stay on pull requests records it in its workflow's row, pr_exempt_jobs (the job names) with pr_exempt_reason, which is also where its cost is argued. Only repos of the Doman-Digital organisation are read (a client's own account pays its own minutes). A local reusable workflow's jobs are judged through the job that calls it; a workflow in another repo is not read.

rules.title: A browser starts on a pull request
rules.why: 15 November 2026 (DOM-17682, Doman-Digital#1777): the monorepo's browser tier (phone-first, website reviews, visual regression, portal journeys) took about 40 minutes of hosted time per run, on every push to every portal pull request. It is queue-only now. The rule fails a job on a pull request that has an unconditional step running Playwright, Chromium, Puppeteer or Cypress (or the repo's .github/actions/playwright), so the pattern cannot come back. Run browsers in the merge queue, on a schedule or by hand, or record a dated exemption in the workflow (# dd: allow CI-038 until=YYYY-MM-DD reason). Unlike the other four, this one is enforced from 13 December: on 15 November six repos (the monorepo's dd-checks-test.yml and five others) already start a browser on pull requests and each needs a decision, not a row. Workflows called from other repos are not read.

rules.title: A macOS job runs on push or pull request
rules.why: 15 November 2026 (DOM-17682): macOS minutes are billed at about ten times a Linux minute ($3.53 of November's first 15 days came from 57 of them). The VoiceOver suites (screen-reader.yml in the monorepo and dd-agent-kit) are dispatch-only now. The rule fails a job on a macos runner in a workflow that starts on push, pull_request or pull_request_target, unless an `if:` keeps it to dispatch or a schedule or a dated exemption in the workflow records it (# dd: allow CI-039 until=YYYY-MM-DD reason). A second policy scan on the same commit is already caught by REG-009.

rules.title: A merge-queue browser-tier job does not read CI_RUNNER_BROWSER
rules.why: 17 November 2026 (DOM-17865, founder decision of 16 November): at the 60% spend flip the runner valve moves everything on vars.CI_RUNNER to dd-ci-01, but the monorepo's merge-queue browser tier cannot run there. DOM-17822 measured five proof entries on dd-ci-ephemeral at 148 to 303 minutes against the queue's 90-minute limit, and phone-first at 83 minutes on the box against its 75-minute cap; on GitHub-hosted it passed in 45 minutes (about $0.51 an entry). The valve keeps the org variable CI_RUNNER_BROWSER on ubuntu-latest until the $0 stop (dd-repo-registry ci-runner-valve.yaml, mode pinned_hosted). The rule fails a job named "queue" in a workflow's TIERS map (or a job of a local reusable workflow it calls) whose runs-on does not read vars.CI_RUNNER_BROWSER, in a workflow that starts on merge_group. Use runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER_BROWSER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}; a deliberate exception is a dated allow comment. Known gap: in hosted mode the valve has no pool-health or canary check until the controller Worker exists (DOM-17692).

rules.title: A pull request or merge-queue job over ten minutes has no expected duration
rules.why: 17 November 2026 (DOM-17629, CI audit gap 3): CI-003 refuses a job with no timeout and CI-037 a job over ten minutes on every pull request push, but a job that is allowed there (verify, build) or runs only in the merge queue (phone-first, 48 minutes of a 65 to 75 minute cap) had no stated length. It could double under its cap and only the bill would show it, weeks later. A job on pull_request, pull_request_target or merge_group whose timeout-minutes (or the largest number in a runner-aware cap) is over 10 has its expected minutes in dd-ci-standards budget.yml, in its workflow's row as job_minutes ("job=minutes, other job=minutes", the measured median), or a cap of 10 or less. The expected figure must be above 0 and no higher than the cap, and a figure for a job that is gone is refused, so a stale number cannot hide. The daily ledger in dd-repo-registry reads the same figures and raises BUD-002 when a job's 7-day median is more than 30 percent over them, so the number lives in one place. Only repos of the Doman-Digital organisation are read. Warn from 17 November, enforced from 1 December.

rules.title: A workflow still uses Vercel
rules.why: Vercel was retired for CI and deploys (DOM-555, DOM-776). On 19 October 2026 its leftovers were still in five repos: six VERCEL_TOKEN_* inputs in dd-repo-registry's sweep, a kv.vercel-storage placeholder in the monorepo's lighthouse.yml, and comments in three other repos describing Vercel building main. A workflow that names Vercel either does nothing or depends on an account nobody watches. A portal still served by Vercel records it as an exemption.

rules.title: Something is set to stay awake with no dated reason
rules.why: 17 November 2026 (DOM-17629, DOM-17703): Meridian's API container was held awake around the clock by a keep-warm cron every 15 minutes, billing for an instance that was idle nearly all day, and nothing in the repo recorded why. Meridian's own test now refuses the switch without a dated reason; this makes that the house rule for every repo. Three things need a dated reason on the same line or the line above (`# YYYY-MM-DD <issue>: <why it must stay awake>`): a keep-warm or keep-alive switch set on (a KEEP_WARM or KEEP_ALIVE key set to 1, true, yes or on, in a workflow, a composite action or a Wrangler config); a cron more often than every 30 minutes (a workflow `schedule:` cron, or a Wrangler `crons` entry in a config that declares a container: a Worker cron on its own is an ordinary poller and is not read, but one in front of a container is the keep-warm ping); and a minimum instance count above zero (min_instances, minInstances, min-instances or min_machines_running). The list is short and exact on purpose: a cron every 30 minutes or less often, a switch set to 0 or false, and a count of 0 are never read. An expression such as `KEEP_WARM: ${{ inputs.warm }}` is not read either. The date is when the reason was written, so a reviewer can ask whether it still holds. Warn from 17 November, enforced from 1 December.

rules.title: A workflow names one of the old persistent runners
rules.why: The eight persistent runners on dd-ci-01 (dd-ci-01-a to dd-ci-01-h) were replaced by a fresh VM per job (DOM-555). On 19 October 2026 a client repo and the monorepo's lighthouse.yml still branched on their names, so the branch never ran and the comment beside it described a machine that is gone. CI-016 catches the workarounds by shape; this catches the names.

rules.title: A declared price per run is far from the measured one
rules.why: 17 November 2026 (DOM-17629, CI audit gap 2): budget.yml declared the monorepo's ci.yml at $0.0292 a run, a sampled mean scaled by 0.11, and the envelope test passed on it. Measured from the runs and jobs APIs (and matched to the billing rows within 1% on 16 and 17 November) a run cost about $0.157, five times the declared figure, so the 60% limit was being checked against a number that was never true. The test compares declared numbers only, so nothing could notice. A workflows: row may now record the measured price: measured_per_run_usd (dollars for one run, blended across the row's events, cancelled runs included), measured_on (YYYY-MM-DD) and measured_basis (how). When it does, per_run_usd must be within 50% of it, or the rule fires. The daily ledger in dd-repo-registry measures the same figure live for every watched workflow (BUD-004, published in ledger.json as workflow_costs) and compares it with per_run_usd with the same 50% band, so a measured_per_run_usd that was edited to match a wrong declaration is still seen. Only the organisation's own repos are read. Raising a repo's ceiling_usd is the founder's decision and is not changed by this rule. Warn from 17 November, enforced from 1 December.

rules.title: A monorepo's pull request job runs every workspace
rules.why: DOM-776 step 5, 19 October 2026: the monorepo's verify and build ran lint, typecheck, test and build for all ten workspaces on every pull request, 22 of its 32 VM-minutes per run, though most PRs touch one app. dd-ci-standards' workspace-scope action works out the affected workspaces (and runs everything when a shared file changes), so a turbo run on a PR passes its filters.

rules.title: budget.yml registers a schedule the repo no longer has
rules.why: DOM-776 step 5, 19 October 2026: budget.yml still listed seven monorepo crons that #1104 had replaced, and a client site's lighthouse.yml long after the workflow was deleted. CI-007 catches a cron with no line; this catches a line with no cron, so the register stays the truth.

rules.title: A cancellable pull request workflow has a job that runs with always()
rules.why: 20 October 2026 (DOM-776): GitHub still runs an always() job after its run is cancelled, so the monorepo's cancelled PR runs stayed queued for hours waiting for a VM for the All checks passed gate, holding the concurrency group, while the newer commit's run sat pending behind them (Doman-Digital#1167, run 39344916461, queued from 23:59 to past 12:40). With if: ${{ !cancelled() }} a cancelled run reports the gate cancelled, tested on 20 October, and a cancelled required check still blocks the merge.

rules.title: A job uses CI_RUNNER_HOSTED without being in hosted-jobs.json (or is listed and does not)
rules.why: DOM-1079, 20 October 2026: the Enterprise plan includes 50,000 GitHub-hosted minutes a month, on an Actions budget of $0 with stop usage on. The whole monorepo would use all of them, so only the jobs listed in dd-ci-standards hosted-jobs.json run there, as runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER_HOSTED || vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}. The runner valve (dd-repo-registry ci-runner-valve.yml, off the boxes it watches) points the variable back at dd-ci-ephemeral at 90% of the allowance. A job on the variable that is not listed spends minutes nobody measured; a listed job that left it reserves minutes for nothing.

rules.title: A third-party action is not pinned to a full commit SHA
rules.why: tj-actions/changed-files, March 2025: a re-pointed tag ran code that dumped CI secrets. GitHub: a full SHA is the only immutable reference. First-party Doman-Digital actions stay on tags.

rules.title: A pnpm repo is missing install protections
rules.why: The 2025 npm worms spread through install scripts and fresh releases. pnpm 10 and later block dependency install scripts unless listed; this rule requires minimumReleaseAge and forbids dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds.

rules.title: No dependency updates configured
rules.why: Security fixes reach a repo only through Renovate (extending this repo's default.json) or Dependabot.

rules.title: A file of secrets is tracked by git
rules.why: 4 October 2026: a pulled env file with 66 production values sat on a client repo's main branch for six months. The CI secret scan only read each push's own commits, so nothing ever looked at it.

rules.title: .gitignore does not cover env and token files
rules.why: 4 October 2026: 12 repos had no .env rule and most client repos did not ignore .doppler-token, while a bulk `git add` stages everything.

rules.title: Nothing scans pull requests for secrets
rules.why: 4 October 2026: GitHub secret scanning is a paid add-on for private repos and was off everywhere; a live Stripe key reached a pushed branch the same day.

rules.title: A Cloudflare deploy reads its token from a GitHub secret
rules.why: 6 and 7 October 2026: the security review found broad, non-expiring Cloudflare tokens hand-copied into repo secrets, where nothing rotates or audits them. Since 13 October 2026 (DOM-776) Workers deploy from Actions through cloudflare-deploy.yml, which fetches a narrow, expiring, per-account token from Doppler with the repo's GitHub identity. Simple static client sites may instead deploy through Cloudflare's GitHub app (Workers Builds), which leaves no token with us.

rules.title: A workflow has no explicit top-level token permissions
rules.why: DOM-776 audit pattern15: workflows inherited unspecified repository token permissions. Declare the minimum top-level permissions (an empty map is valid), and grant any extra permission only to the job that needs it.

rules.title: A workflow signs in to Doppler with the repo's identity, which is missing or unregistered
rules.why: 14 to 21 October 2026 (DOM-1265): a client site's Deploy failed on every run for a week with "Input required and not supplied: doppler-identity-id", because the repo never had the DOPPLER_IDENTITY_ID variable, and nothing noticed. The nine repos that worked had their identities made and their variables set by hand from a script outside Git. dd-repo-registry doppler-identities.json now records every repo's identity, and doppler-identities.json here is its projection (DOM-1643: repo and identity as sha256 hashes, because this repo is public); this rule fails a repo whose workflows sign in without a row there, with a row that records no identity, without the variable, or with a different value. 17 November 2026 (DOM-17914): dd-repo-registry signed in with `doppler oidc login` from a run step, a null row and no variable for weeks, because the rule only saw the action input and the shared deploy; it now sees the command line too and fails a null row wherever the doctor runs. The variable is read by the policy job in the repo's own Actions run.

rules.title: A pull request adds a client's, a client's person's or a staff member's name to a public org repo
rules.why: 29 to 31 October 2026 (DOM-1643): the two public org repos carried a map of every client, Worker and Doppler identity, and prose and fixtures that named clients, their people and our staff. A public repo publishes its history for good, and taking names out of it means a history rewrite and a GitHub Support request. The founder asked for prevention as well as the clean-up. This fails a pull request into a public Doman-Digital repo when its diff, a path it adds, a commit message, its title or its description holds a name on the list. The list is kept in the private dd-repo-registry; this repo holds public-names.json, salted sha256 hashes of each name's forms and the allowlisted lines with their reasons, so the check names nobody and runs on pull requests from forks, which get no secret. The same list feeds the kit's pre-push hook and the registry sweep (PUB-002 to PUB-004). Name a client by its trade and a person by their role. A merge queue run is not checked: it has no pull request in its event, and the pull request was.

rules.title: A Worker has no registered deploy path, or two
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): some Workers were built by Cloudflare's GitHub app, some by Actions, and seven repos had no trace of how they deploy. dd-repo-registry deploys.json lists every Worker with its one path, and deploys.json here is its projection (DOM-1643: repo and Worker as sha256 hashes, because this repo is public): Actions (cloudflare-deploy.yml) for internal Workers and anything gated, or retired. From 29 October 2026 client sites move off Workers Builds to Actions too, so every client deploy runs after CI with a narrow token per client (DOM-1644).

rules.title: A Worker cron has no registry row with the same schedule
rules.why: 9 November 2026: a cron in a Worker's wrangler config runs whether or not anyone registered it, so nothing counted what it woke. Every trigger in wrangler.jsonc or wrangler.toml needs a cf.* row in dd-repo-registry jobs/ whose defined_in names this file and whose schedule is the same string. This is CI-007 for Actions crons, checked against the registry rather than budget.yml.

rules.title: A job that runs more often than every 15 minutes and reads Neon has no db_gate
rules.why: 9 November 2026: Neon suspends a database after about five quiet minutes, so a job that runs more often than every 15 minutes and touches Postgres keeps the compute awake all day. A cf.* row whose schedule is more frequent than every 15 minutes and whose database is a Neon project id must name in db_gate the cheap check that runs before Postgres (a due-time check in the Worker's own state, a cache, or a no-op when nothing has changed). Every row needs a database field, a Neon project id or none.

rules.title: The repo runs a craft catalogue older than copy-check trusts
rules.why: 19 October 2026: copy-check passed a client email full of chatbot residue because the machine ran craft catalogue 2026.09.12. Repos were worse: their lockfiles held craft 0.5.0 to 0.20.2 (catalogues none to 2026.10.2) while npm had 0.20.5, because Renovate aborted every repo before opening a PR (DOM-1043). The floor is floors.json, the same number copy-check refuses below. Renovate's house packages group bumps craft within a day of a release; a repo still behind fails here rather than checking copy with old rules.

rules.title: A nested pnpm lockfile sits inside the root workspace without being one of its packages
rules.why: 21 October 2026: Renovate's house packages PR on a client site bumped astro/package.json but not astro/pnpm-lock.yaml, and every Workers Build of the live site failed until #731 (DOM-1273). astro/ is installed with --ignore-workspace, but Renovate runs `pnpm install --lockfile-only` in the folder with no way to add that flag, so pnpm installed the root workspace, exited 0 and left the nested lockfile stale. A nested project outside the root workspace gets its own pnpm-workspace.yaml (`packages: []`), as osint-engine and three client repos already do; with it the same command updates the right lockfile.

rules.title: A pull request names no Linear issue
rules.why: 20 October 2026: client work was shipping with nothing in Linear or HubSpot to show for it. Since 22 July, 640 of 869 pull requests merged into the client repos named no issue, so the founder could not see what had been done for whom (DOM-1100). Every pull request names its issue: a `Closes DOM-123` or `Part of DOM-123` line (CRO-7 works too) in the title or description, or the key at the start of the branch name (dom-123-short-name), read the way dd-relay reads them when it moves Linear on a merge. A key mentioned in passing does not count (27 October 2026, DOM-1363: the relay ignores it). Work with no issue carries the no-issue label. Renovate and Dependabot branches are exempt, and so are changeset-release/ branches: the Changesets Version Packages PR names no issue by design and its bot rewrites the title and body, so a label added after it opens came too late and a new Version PR stayed red until the next push to main (17 November 2026). After fixing the description or adding the label, push a commit (an empty one will do): editing does not start the check again, and a re-run reads the old description (probed 27 October 2026).

rules.title: A pull request quotes a closing word beside an issue it does not own
rules.why: 26 October 2026: dd-claude-kit#178 quoted another PR's `Closes DOM-1014` line, and Linear closed DOM-1014 when #178 merged. The Linear GitHub app, installed on the whole org, reads closing words anywhere in a title or description, inside backticks, code blocks and quotes too (DOM-1363). A closing word in a quote beside a key the pull request does not claim (a Closes or Part of line outside the quote, or the branch) is flagged so the author can rewrite it as `names DOM-n` before the merge.

rules.title: The repo's description or tags break repo-topics.json
rules.why: Every repo must be identifiable from its GitHub page alone, and its kind tag decides which rules apply (was the repo metadata check, enforced since September 2026).

rules.title: The repo has workflows but nothing runs the policy check
rules.why: 3 October 2026: 14 of 48 repos with workflows were checked by nothing. Since 27 October 2026 the org ruleset dd-policy-required runs the check on every private Doman-Digital repo with no caller, so a caller is required only where it does not apply: public repos and repos on other accounts (DOM-17635). Read from the default branch's live rules, or, when they cannot be read, from who org-rulesets.yaml covers.

rules.title: The repo calls the policy check the org ruleset already runs
rules.why: 14 November 2026 (DOM-17635): the monorepo ran the scan twice on every commit, once as `policy / check` from its caller and once as `check` from dd-policy-required, as did 13 other covered repos. The second run costs a runner and a checkout per commit and puts two policy results in the checks list. Only the live rules count here: a repo the registry leaves out has no ruleset run, and its caller is its only scan.

rules.title: Auto-merge or delete-branch-on-merge is off
rules.why: 7 October 2026: pull requests are assessed and merged by agents, with the required checks as the only gate (DOM-443). Auto-merge lets a PR merge itself the moment its checks pass, and deleting the branch on merge stops merged branches piling up. Both are repo settings, read from GitHub; when the settings cannot be read, nothing is checked. Auto-merge is not required on a private repo in a personal account, where GitHub's Free plan ignores it; delete-branch-on-merge still is.

rules.title: The ruleset requires a check no workflow produces
rules.why: DOM-776 step 5, 19 October 2026: a client repo's ruleset required `scan`, the job of gitleaks.yml, which the step was about to delete. A required check that never reports holds every pull request open with no error to read. The estate sweep and the policy check read the default branch's rules and compare them with the jobs the workflows define.

rules.title: The default branch has a merge queue and a required check's workflow does not run on merge_group
rules.why: DOM-1262, 21 October 2026: dd-claude-kit, dd-repo-registry and dd-relay moved from "must be up to date with main" to a merge queue once the org was on Enterprise Cloud. The queue tests each pull request on its own merge_group run and waits for the required checks there; a workflow without the trigger never reports, so the queue holds every pull request until it times out, with no error on the pull request. The policy check and the estate sweep read the default branch's rules and the workflows that produce each required check.

rules.title: An exemption expires within 14 days, is invalid, or exempts nothing
rules.why: Exemptions expire so ignored debt comes back as a finding instead of a forgotten note. One that matches no finding hides the next real one unreviewed (DOM-776 audit, 13 October 2026: dd-seo-mcp, dd-repo-registry and dd-prompt-library carried exemptions for findings already fixed).

rules.title: The repo pins dd-ci-standards to one release instead of v1
rules.why: 13 October 2026 (DOM-776): Renovate rewrote @v1 to fixed releases. policy.yml itself ran the doctor at v1.0.13 from 5 October, so every PR gate missed SEC-007, REG-004 and the CI-001 fixes while v1 had moved on to v1.0.22.

rules.title: A shared workflow or action is pinned to a branch
rules.why: 19 October 2026 (DOM-776): dd-photo-pack called the policy workflow at @dom-776-ci-deploy-standards, a working branch. A branch moves without a release and vanishes when it is merged and deleted, and then every run of the caller fails. Pin a house workflow or action to a major tag (@v1), a release or a full commit SHA.
